title: Lorenz at the Hunting Ground
sceneText:
He is not hunting and he is not on a horse; he came on foot. You did not expect to meet a Forge-keeper at the hunting ground.

Lorenz has gone out to the edge of the woods and stopped beside a big oak, with his hand on the bark. His back is very quiet.

He hears you come up and does not turn round.

{@lorenz}“You came.”

“I thought you did not attend the season.”

{@lorenz}“I do not,” he says. “I came for this tree.”

You ask what is particular about the tree.

{@lorenz}“The tinder for the Kindling is taken from here,” he says. “All three estates take theirs from here: Maplegate, Thornwall, Millridge.”

He takes his hand off the bark.

{@lorenz}“But it is not cut. We take only what it drops of itself. However much comes down in a given autumn is what we take, and in a year when little comes down the three houses divide it.”

“Why this one?”

{@lorenz}“It has always been this one.”

He looks up at the crown.

{@lorenz}“A good deal has come down this year. It is a good year.”

He walks half a circle round the tree, picks up a fallen branch, weighs it, and puts it down again. He says something, in a language you do not understand.

The Master turns, sees you puzzled, and says it again in the common tongue.

{@lorenz}“The seasons turn, and the fire is kindled again. The first snow is near, and the Sacred Flame will shine again on this land.”

variants.lorenz_question:
He picks up a second fallen branch.

{@lorenz}“Last autumn, at the taking of the wood, a man came to find me,” he says. “Here.”

You wait.

{@lorenz}“He asked me,” he says, flicking a little soil off the branch with a finger, “whether, if the work a man does is itself wrong, doing that work better means being further in the wrong.”

Lorenz puts the branch into the cloth bag at his side.

{@lorenz}“He asked it very politely, as though it were something with nothing to do with him.”

He looks up at you.

{@lorenz}“But a technical question, asked by that man, is not a technical question any more.”

“What did you tell him?”

{@lorenz}“I did not answer him,” he says. “I had no answer that could meet it. But I should have asked him then why he was asking.”

He draws the mouth of the bag closed.

{@lorenz}“I did not ask.”
variants.lorenz_question_again:
He picks up the second fallen branch and weighs it in his hand.

{@lorenz}“I have told you about what he came and asked me.”

You say you remember.

{@lorenz}“It was here.” With the hand holding the branch he points at the ground. “This spot. Where he stood that day was a little to the left of where you are standing now.”

He puts the branch into the bag.

{@lorenz}“I have thought about it many times this year,” he says. “Not about what he asked.”

{@lorenz}“About why I did not ask him.”
variants.marguerite_open:
On the way back to camp, Marguerite’s carriage is standing at the side of the forest road. She is sitting inside with the door open.

{@marguerite}“Come up and sit a while.”

It is warmer inside than out. She moves the rug on her knees aside.

The carriage starts.
variants.marguerite_thanks: {@marguerite}“Last night,” she says. “You need not feel you owe me anything. Henk has to do that once a year, and somebody always has to head him off.”
variants.marguerite_clue:
She looks out of the window.

{@marguerite}“Hartmann came to me as well.”

She says it in exactly the tone she used a moment ago, as though speaking about the trees along the road.

{@marguerite}“Late August. He came without sending word first, which was unlike him. I had tea brought, and he sat over an hour.”

“What did he say?”

{@marguerite}“He did not say,” she says. “He went round it a long while, asking about matters of estate management, very politely and very unnecessarily. He knew those things better than I do.”

{@marguerite}“I waited for him to bring out the real thing. He did not, not until the sun went down.”

The wheels go over a stretch of loose stone. She puts a hand to the window frame.

{@marguerite}“At the end he stood up and thanked me and said he had disturbed me.”

She turns her head to look at you.

{@marguerite}“I am still thinking about it,” she says. “What that young man wanted to ask was not a question I could answer.”

“What question?”

{@marguerite}“I do not know,” she says. “But that he came to me means he had already asked others, and that they had not given him an answer either.”

The carriage reaches the camp turning. She raps twice on the panel and it stops.

{@marguerite}“He was a good family steward,” she says. “Nobody in this part of the country ever doubted that.”

“Including him?”

She looks at you a while.

{@marguerite}“That is the question.”
